title: Collect the complete VCF Operations for Networks problem event page-through in a stable order
prompt:
Implement `vcfnetworks/client.go` as a standard-library-only Go client that retrieves the complete VCF Operations for Networks 9.1 problem event collection. Add no dependencies. You may also add table-driven tests in `vcfnetworks/client_test.go`; do not edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection derived directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/vcf-operations-for-networks-openapi.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable VCF 9.1 release commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`. `docs/official_sources.json` records that commit, the exact specification path, and every operationId in the projection. No rendered documentation page is a contract source. Use only the specification operationIds `listProblemEvents` (`GET /entities/problems`) and `getProblemEvent` (`GET /entities/problems/{id}`), both under the specification server root `/api/ni`.

Preserve the supplied public API: `NewClient(baseURL, apiToken string, httpClient *http.Client) (*Client, error)`, `(*Client).CollectProblemEvents(ctx context.Context, options CollectOptions) ([]ProblemEvent, error)`, `ProblemEvent`, `CollectOptions`, `APIError`, and `ProtocolError`. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Reject a non-HTTP(S) service root, a service root without a host or carrying a query or fragment, and a blank or header-unsafe API token. Validate `CollectOptions` before issuing any request: reject a nil context, a `Size` outside 1 through 1000, an `EventStatus` outside `open`, `closed`, `all`, an `EventSeverity` entry outside `Critical`, `Warning`, `Moderate`, `Info`, an empty `EventType`, an empty `EventTags` or `Managers` entry, and a negative epoch. No error may disclose the API token.

Every request is a bodyless GET carrying exactly one `Authorization: NetworkInsight <api_token>` and one `Accept: application/json`, with no `Content-Type`, body, transfer encoding, or positive content length. Build query strings with `url.Values` and `Encode`, so members are alphabetically ordered and normally escaped, and emit no bare `?`.

Apart from the page size every `listProblemEvents` parameter is optional, so `CollectOptions` uses pointers and slices to distinguish a value the caller supplied from an unset one. Omit every nil pointer and empty slice completely: `start_time`, `end_time`, `event_type`, `event_tags`, `event_status`, `update_time_from`, `update_time_to`, `event_severity`, `managers`, and the `getProblemEvent` `time` parameter. Never serialize an unset field as an empty string, zero, false, `null`, or an empty placeholder. Preserve explicitly supplied values, including an epoch of `0` and an `EventStatus` of `all` even though `all` is the schema default. `event_tags`, `event_severity` and `managers` are `style=form, explode=true` arrays, so each element becomes its own repeated key rather than one joined value. Send `size` on every page request and add only `cursor` for pagination; carry the caller's filters unchanged on every page and invent no other server filter or sort control.

Drain the collection with the specification's opaque cursor: the first request carries no `cursor` at all, and each later request replays the preceding response's `cursor` verbatim until a response omits it. Treat only exact HTTP 200 as success and require a JSON media type. Each page must carry a non-null `results` array and a non-negative integer `total_count` that never changes between pages, every result must have a nonblank `entity_id` and `entity_type` of `ProblemEvent`, no page may exceed the requested size, a non-final page must be full, and the server must not repeat a cursor. Cursor windows may overlap, so the same `entity_id` can appear on more than one page: keep the first sighting and count each entity once. When the drain ends, the number of distinct entities must equal `total_count`.

Resolve every distinct entity through exactly one `getProblemEvent` call, in the order the entities first appeared, and reject a detail body that answers a different `entity_id`, omits `name`, or reports an `entity_type` other than `ProblemEvent`. Return fresh `ProblemEvent` values sorted ascending by `Name`, then by case-sensitive `EntityID`, independent of server page order. Decode a non-200 JSON `ApiError` into `*APIError` with `StatusCode`, `Code`, and `Message`; malformed success bodies and pagination violations use `*ProtocolError` with a reason. Buffer the collection and return a nil slice rather than partial results on every failure.

Run `go test -race ./...`.
scenario: The listProblemEvents collection spans three opaque cursor pages whose windows overlap, so one entity is served twice and the seven distinct events arrive out of order and must be counted once, resolved individually through getProblemEvent, and returned completely in a deterministic client-side order.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves the exact bodyless GET wire shape, including complete omission of every unset optional query field rather than an empty or default representation, and exploded repeated keys for the array-valued filters.
